title: Merge Intervals
statement:
You are given `n` closed intervals `[start_i, end_i]` in no particular order.

Two intervals **overlap** if they share at least one point. This includes intervals that only touch at an endpoint: `[1, 4]` and `[4, 7]` overlap at `4`. Overlap is chained: if A overlaps B and B overlaps C, all three belong to the same merged interval, even if A and C do not overlap directly.

Merge every group of overlapping intervals into a single interval that spans from the smallest start to the largest end in the group, and return the resulting non-overlapping intervals **sorted by start** in increasing order. Together they must cover exactly the same points as the input.
inputFormat:
The first line contains an integer `n`.
Each of the next `n` lines contains two integers `start_i end_i`.
outputFormat: Print the merged intervals in increasing order of start, one per line, as two space-separated integers `start end`.

examples.explanation: Sorted by start: [1,3], [2,5], [8,12], [11,14], [17,17]. [1,3] and [2,5] share points 2–3 and merge into [1,5]. [8,12] and [11,14] share 11–12 and merge into [8,14]. [17,17] overlaps nothing and stays as it is.
[3,6] and [6,9] touch at 6, which counts as overlapping, so they merge into [3,9]. [0,2] ends at 2 and the next interval starts at 3; they share no point, so [0,2] stays separate.
[5,6] and [10,11] lie inside [2,20], and [15,25] overlaps it on 15–20, so everything merges into [2,25].

hints: If the intervals are sorted by start, which ones can possibly overlap the interval you are currently building?
Scan the sorted intervals keeping one open merged interval. A new interval either extends it (its start is at most the current end) or closes it and starts a new one.
When extending, take the maximum of the two ends: a later interval can sit entirely inside the current one.

def gen(rng):
    def fmt(iv):
        return f'{len(iv)}\n' + '\n'.join(f'{s} {e}' for s, e in iv)

    def rand(n, hi, maxlen):
        out = []
        for _ in range(n):
            s = rng.randint(0, hi)
            out.append((s, min(hi, s + rng.randint(0, maxlen))))
        return out

    tests = [
        fmt([(0, 0)]),
        fmt([(10000, 10000)]),
        fmt([(5, 5), (5, 5), (5, 5)]),
        fmt([(1, 3), (3, 5)]),
        fmt([(4, 6), (1, 2)]),
        fmt([(2, 2), (2, 9), (9, 9)]),
        fmt([(0, 10000), (3, 4), (100, 200), (9999, 10000)]),
        fmt([(6, 7), (4, 5), (2, 3), (0, 1)]),
        fmt([(0, 2), (1, 4), (3, 6), (5, 8), (7, 10)]),
    ]
    for n, hi, ml in [(3, 10, 3), (5, 15, 4), (6, 20, 2), (8, 30, 5), (10, 40, 6), (12, 25, 3), (15, 60, 4), (20, 100, 8), (25, 50, 1)]:
        tests.append(fmt(rand(n, hi, ml)))
    # large
    tests.append(fmt(rand(10000, 10000, 3)))
    iv = [(i, i) for i in range(0, 10000, 2)] + [(i, i) for i in range(0, 10000, 2)]
    rng.shuffle(iv)
    tests.append(fmt(iv))
    iv = [(i % 5000, 10000 - i % 5000) for i in range(10000)]
    rng.shuffle(iv)
    tests.append(fmt(iv))
    tests.append(fmt(rand(10000, 10000, 0)))
    return tests
